rationale: Two payload fields this lane published nothing for, and one of them was actively misleading. `line_number` was absent on ALL 9,132 relationships the analyzer emitted over its own pinned corpus, while 35 of 41 analyzers publish it and `context.mdInlineLines` -- which the engine computes for precisely this purpose and handed over on the analyze context -- was read by nobody. Its absence had three measured consequences: bb_graph's line-guarded caller/callee dedup (graph-engine.ts) skips every markdown edge, bb_doc renders markdown citations with no `#L` anchor (85% NULL, the worst language in the index), and the store's relationship primary key `(source, type, target, line)` could not tell two call sites of one target apart, which is what made the code-block identity defect unrecoverable. `evidenceClass` was absent too, and the read-time derivation in graph-core.ts does not list `contains` among its structural types, so the heading hierarchy -- a direct AST parent/child relation, the one edge class in this lane that cannot be a guess -- was rendered to readers as `inferred`: 'a guess, treat as a hint, never as fact'. Both are now assigned centrally, so an emission site cannot skip them. The line conversion for an inline edge is the one non-obvious part and it is pinned here: the engine sub-parses each `inline` node as a SUBSTRING, so a node row inside that tree is relative to the substring and the file line is `mdInlineLines[i] + row`. The reference link at L28 is the assertion for that arithmetic, because its destination comes from a block-level definition rather than from the node it is attributed to.

_everyRelationshipCarries.note: asserted by the lane census over its pinned corpus (scala3@18df09c0, 738 tracked .md files): 11,401/11,401 relationships carry a 1-based line_number and an evidenceClass from the closed vocabulary. Before this round it was 0/9,132.

_seamNote.what: `expectUniqueIds` is NOT used by this lane and cannot be.
_seamNote.why: The runner reads `symbol.id`, but markdown's symbols reach it through pool-worker's BasicSymbol projection, which does not carry `id` -- every symbol arrives with `id === undefined`, so a uniqueness check over two sites would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with identity. Site uniqueness is instead carried by the store's own `(file_id, name, start_line)` key, which the site-keyed analyzer now feeds distinct start lines for.

_payloadNote.range: pinned by the `expectSymbolRanges` channel above (the runner's real one — this entry first named a singular `expectSymbolRange` that does not exist, and section C reads a named key, so an invented key is indistinguishable from an unpinned one). The lines are 1-BASED per M59 #825, and the store's `(file_id, name, line_start)` key is what makes two sites of one construct distinct rows — the mechanism the code-block identity fix depends on, so the range is pinned rather than assumed.
_payloadNote.visibility: every markdown symbol is `public`: a document has no private or package scope, so the field is CONSTANT rather than absent, and a constant is pinned like any other value because a regression that dropped it would be invisible.
_payloadNote.ownerName: pinned on the expectSymbols entries above, and the case that broke it — a repeated heading's children attaching to the wrong occurrence — is pinned by heading-identity's forbid half instead.
